User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the CongreKids application, holding their profile information and assigned role.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

displayName.description: The user's display name from their authentication provider.

photoURL.description: URL to the user's profile picture.

role.description: The user's assigned role in the application ('parent' or 'admin').

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

Child.title: Child
Child.description: Represents a child associated with a specific parent user for childcare registrations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Child entity within a parent's profile.

userId.description: Reference to the parent User. (Relationship: User 1:N Child)

Meeting.title: Meeting
Meeting.description: Details of a parent meeting, including registration information and childcare age groups.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Meeting entity.

title.description: The title or name of the meeting.

date.description: The date and time of the meeting.

registrationDeadline.description: The deadline for parents to register their children for this meeting.

status.description: The current status of the meeting registration ('upcoming', 'closed', 'past').

ageGroups.description: An array of age group objects, each with 'label' (string), 'minMonths' (number), and 'maxMonths' (number). Defines the age ranges for childcare at this meeting.

createdBy.description: Reference to the User who created the meeting. (Relationship: User 1:N Meeting)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the meeting was created.

Registration.title: Registration
Registration.description: Records a parent's sign-up for a specific meeting, detailing their children attending.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Registration entity (typically the parent's user ID for the meeting).

meetingId.description: Reference to the Meeting this registration is for. (Relationship: Meeting 1:N Registration)

parentId.description: Reference to the parent User who made this registration. (Relationship: User 1:N Registration)

parentName.description: The display name of the parent who registered.

parentEmail.description: The email address of the parent who registered.

children.description: An array of children registered by this parent for this specific meeting. Each item is an object with 'childId' (string), 'name' (string), 'birthDate' (date-time string), and 'ageGroupLabel' (string).

registeredAt.description: Timestamp when this registration was first created.

lastUpdatedAt.description: Timestamp when this registration was last modified.

cancelledChildren.description: (Optional) An array tracking children whose registration was cancelled. Each item is an object with 'childId' (string), 'name' (string), and 'cancelledAt' (date-time string).

definition.description: Stores core user profile data, including their display name, email, and role. Ownership is path-based, with `{userId}` matching `request.auth.uid`. The 'role' field is for client-side display; admin authorization is handled by the separate `/roles_admin/{adminId}` collection.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of the user.

definition.description: A dedicated collection for robust admin role authorization. Documents in this collection exist only for users with the 'admin' role. Security rules will use `exists(/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))` for atomic admin checks, ensuring Authorization Independence and adhering to DBAC principles.

params.name: adminId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of an administrator user.

definition.description: Stores individual child profiles, owned by the parent specified by `{userId}`. This path ensures strong ownership-based security. Authorization is independent as `{userId}` must match `request.auth.uid`.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of the parent user.

params.name: childId
params.description: The unique identifier for the child within the parent's collection.

definition.description: Stores details for each childcare meeting. Documents are publicly readable by all authenticated users for listing and viewing. Write access is restricted to administrators (checked via `/roles_admin/{adminId}`).

params.name: meetingId
params.description: The unique identifier for the meeting.

definition.description: Records a parent's registration for a specific meeting. The `{parentId}` in the path matches `request.auth.uid` for parent access control. Includes denormalized 'parentName' and 'parentEmail' from the User entity for Authorization Independence, enabling display without additional `get()` calls.

params.name: meetingId
params.description: The unique identifier of the meeting this registration is for.

params.name: parentId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of the parent who made the registration.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and debuggable, adhering strictly to the core design principles and strategy mandates. 

**Authorization Independence:**
1.  **User and Child Data:** For `/users/{userId}` and `/users/{userId}/children/{childId}`, ownership is inherently tied to the path. `request.auth.uid` must match `{userId}` in the path, eliminating the need for `get()` calls to verify ownership. This makes rules for personal data simple and atomic.
2.  **Admin Roles (DBAC):** To achieve true authorization independence for admin checks, a separate `/roles_admin/{adminId}` collection is introduced. Instead of checking a `role` field within a user document (which would require a `get()` call), security rules can perform an `exists()` check on `/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid)`. This operation is atomic, robust, and directly aligns with the DBAC principle of 'Existence over Content', making admin authorization checks highly efficient and debuggable.
3.  **Registrations:** For `/meetings/{meetingId}/registrations/{parentId}`, the `parentId` in the path directly corresponds to the `request.auth.uid` of the parent making the registration. This ensures parents can only access their own registration documents atomically. Furthermore, key parent information (`parentName`, `parentEmail`) is denormalized directly into the registration document. This avoids `get()` calls to the `/users` collection when admins or the UI need to display registration details, enhancing performance and rule simplicity.

**QAPs (Query/Access Pattern Support):**
1.  **Users and Children:** Parents can securely query and manage their own children under `/users/{userId}/children`. Admins, with their dedicated role access, can read all `/users` data and their subcollections.
2.  **Meetings:** The `/meetings/{meetingId}` collection is designed for public read access by all authenticated users, allowing them to `list` upcoming and past meetings efficiently without complex rule filtering. Write access is strictly limited to authenticated administrators, verified through the `/roles_admin/{adminId}` existence check.
3.  **Registrations:** Parents can view and modify their *own* registrations for specific meetings by referencing `/meetings/{meetingId}/registrations/$(request.auth.uid)`. To view a list of all their historical registrations across meetings, a collection group query on `registrations` where `parentId == request.auth.uid` can be securely executed. Admins can `list` all registrations for any given meeting, as they have full read access to meeting subcollections. This structure allows for secure `list` operations without relying on rules as filters.
